Release Notes:
# Adjutant AI (formerly AI Workbench) — Release notes, full history Every release in full: what is new, what changed and what was fixed, with the reasons. The short summary for each release is on the Splunkbase listing. **App version:** 2.8.0 **Last updated:** 2026-11-10 > **About version numbers.** Releases once numbered 0.10–0.13 were renumbered to > 1.0–1.3 to reflect production maturity — no behaviour changed. The current release is > **2.8.0**, after **2.7.6**, a maintenance release on **2.7.0** after **2.7.1**, **2.7.2**, **2.7.3** and **2.7.5**: Adjutant AI runs **governed agents**, a **Tool calls** panel shows each step of a > request and lets you stop it, and **multi-source reconciliation** arrives as a Preview. > 2.7.0 sits on top of **2.5.9**'s setup wizard that says which model actually answered and why a > gateway lists none, a ninth option for self-hosted and in-house models, and connection checks that > pass only on real proof; 2.5.9 on top of **2.5.8**'s playbooks that carry all of their instructions, and every path to > an AI service agreeing about where a request goes, and 2.5.8 on top of **2.5.4**'s readable RCA report and **2.5.3**'s private LLM endpoints and **2.5.2**'s one connection for several tenants and **2.5.1**'s fixes to **2.5.0**'s setup wizard and **2.4.2** — a data-correctness fix on top of **2.4.1**, a connectivity release on top of the **2.4.0** integration workstream and **2.2.2**, itself a maintenance release on **2.2.1**, itself a maintenance release on > **2.2.0**'s **Explain a SPL search**, and **2.1.0**'s **Fraud capability** and the **2.0 line** (the deterministic **ITSI Root > Cause Analysis** engine, **resource-consumption monitoring**, and **2.0.7**'s durable memory, > Scheduled Ask and governed integrations), which in turn built on > **1.8.5** (the **CIM Coverage Audit**), **1.8.4** (async playbook execution over MCP > plus the **Outcome Ledger** executive/audit dashboard), **1.8.3** > (a security‑hardening release: OWASP + dependency + anti‑ransomware audit), **1.8.2** (Splunk > Edge Processor data‑quality awareness and keyless Azure OpenAI authentication), **1.8.1** > (support‑diagnosis fixes) and **1.8.0** (agent telemetry & OCSF export, content packs, > all‑tiers data‑quality checks, Splunk 10.x readiness, Dashboard Studio version‑awareness). The > **1.7.0** ServiceNow integration and the **1.5.0 "Data Foundation & MCP OAuth"** themes are > included below. --- ## 2.8.0 ### Questions you answer with a click - When the assistant needs a decision, it shows a question card in the reply area instead of ending its answer with a question: up to four questions, choices as buttons with the recommended one first, an **Other…** field on every question, and one click when there is a single choice to make. Text typed in the reply box while a card is open is sent as your answer (**Send as answer**). - **Stop** while a card is open ends the request; the card shows **Not answered**. The TOOL CALLS panel shows the question as a **Your answer** step, and the time strip counts the wait as *Waiting for user*. - A step that asks a question runs nothing else: a search or change the assistant asked for next to the question is shown as *Not run* and is run after your answer if it is still needed, so it never runs before you have answered. - The shipped agent templates, skills and knowledge now ask through the card. An agent running unattended never waits for an answer: it takes the recommended option and says which, and it never makes a change on that basis. ### Your Splunk roles and knowledge objects - **⋮ after your name** in the header lists your Splunk roles, for every user: the roles assigned to you and the ones you inherit through them. What you can share or delete in Splunk depends on these roles. They are read with your own Splunk session. - **⋮ on an object in "Created in Splunk"**: **Visibility…** (laid out like Splunk's *Edit Permissions*: what it is now, *Owner (private)*, *This app* or *All apps* in one row, what saving will do, and the roles that can read or change it) and **Delete…** (after a confirmation that names it). You are offered only what Splunk lets you do, with your own session; an option you can't use says why, and roles already set that you can't change are kept. - **History has two tabs, and opens in every edition.** **Splunk Knowledge Objects** (first) lists every knowledge object you own in the app you opened Adjutant AI from, however it was made: type, visibility, the date in your Splunk time zone, whether Adjutant AI created it, and the same **⋮**. Every column filters and sorts. **Agent History** (the previous History) still needs Professional; on the free tier it says so instead of the tab being greyed out. - **Dashboards, reports and alerts are created as you**, with your own Splunk rights, in every app. Before, a private report in an app other than Adjutant AI's was refused. - **The reply says how an object is shared as Splunk reports it.** A share your role may not make no longer fails the request: the object is kept as it is (usually private: only you can see it) and the reply says it was not shared, in plain words. A dashboard or report that is already yours and private is no longer re-permissioned when you ask for private. - **"Created in Splunk" says who can see each object**: *Private: only you can see it*, with the way to share it (**⋮ › Visibility…**), or *Shared with this app* / *all apps*. A share Splunk refused says why, for example *Sharing with this app needs write permission on the app; ask your administrator.* - **An alert needs the `schedule_search` capability.** Without it the assistant says so before anything is created or changed, and offers a report instead. - A write with no known Splunk user is refused, and nothing is created or changed. - **Fixed:** a dashboard's base searches are saved for a role that may not schedule searches (the `user` role). Before, each one asked to be "not scheduled", which Splunk refuses to such a role, so its searches stayed inline in the dashboard, with a warning. - **Fixed:** a user with only the `user` role, whom an Organisation's patterns match, can use the app. Before, the browser read the Organisations with the user's own session, which the `user` role may not do, so such a user was shown *Adjutant AI is not available for you*. The server now says which Organisation and Business Unit you are in. When it cannot read them, the app says *Adjutant AI could not read your Organisation settings* and asks you to reload; it never says you have no access. - **Fixed:** a tool disabled for an Organisation or Business Unit stays disabled for a user with only the `user` role. Before, that role could not read the tool settings, and the app took the refused read for "nothing disabled". The server now says which tools are disabled for you. When it cannot, no tool is offered or run, and the Console says the tool settings could not be read. ### An agent your licence does not cover never runs - The licence check of an agent template now holds when it RUNS, not only in the list: a scheduled, triggered, MCP, REST or Console start of a template your licence does not cover is refused before any model call, with the same sentence the list shows, and recorded in History. The starts that answer at once (MCP, REST and the Console) refuse it straight away and queue nothing. - Two starts of the same agent in the same Org/BU share one run: the second shows the run that is already in flight, also when both arrive within the same second, also over MCP (it used to answer with an error). - **Changed:** starts are refused while the agent engine is off, instead of queuing a run that never starts: the Change Forensics start, Run now on an agent job, sending an approved write and a flow's Run now say so. The follow-on jobs of a run that ends after the engine was switched off are not started, and that run's record names each one and why; an integration or flow target also shows it as skipped. ### Unattended runs that are not audited are named - On the **Unattended** tab an administrator sees *"Runs are not audited: set an audit index for <Org>."* for their own Org and every Org with a listed job that has no audit index, with a link to that Org in **Orgs & BUs**. Shown where audit logging is licensed; never shown when the Orgs could not be read. ### Changed: scheduled agent jobs record who signed them - When an administrator creates, edits or re-signs a scheduled agent job on the **Unattended** tab, the job records that administrator as its signer, and its signature covers the signer: a signer changed outside the tab stops the job, as any other changed setting does. - Each signing is written to the audit log as a `schedule_signed` event that names the signer, in Orgs with an audit index. - Every job signed on the tab records its signer, including a job you re-sign once after the upgrade (see *Upgrade note: review and re-sign your scheduled jobs once*). ### Upgrade note: Fraud Rule Builder and Fraud Command Center run in the Console only - Both need values only a person can give: the detection threshold, the customer's thresholds and AML jurisdiction lists. They ask for them in the Console every time, and their Agent modes switches are disabled. - **Fraud Rule Builder no longer runs from alerts.** Its Triggered mode is gone. Any mode an install had switched on for either agent is switched off on upgrade, with an `agent_mode_upgrade_conflict` line in the platform audit log. An unattended start is refused before the language model is called. ### Upgrade note: review and re-sign your scheduled jobs once - **Review and re-sign your scheduled jobs once.** Scheduled jobs created before 2.8.0 have no signature, so after the upgrade they do not run until an administrator re-signs them. Open the **Unattended** tab: a notice lists the jobs that do not run, with the Organisation, agent and actions of each. Tick the ones you recognise and choose **Re-sign**; this also restores their permissions. - **A job set up outside the Unattended tab must be recreated there.** This means a saved search to which the scheduled-job action was added by hand, which was never a supported way to schedule a job. It cannot be re-signed. Create the job on the Unattended tab, then delete the old saved search. ### Agents know which indexes you can search, and what is in them - When an agent lists indexes, the list is the one **you** can search: it comes from a search run as you, so it never names an index your roles cannot read. Metric and empty indexes are included. - On a large estate an agent finds any index by a name pattern (for example `fw_*`). A list longer than 200 indexes says it was cut short, gives the total, and the agent narrows it with a pattern. - A daily **index catalogue** tells the agent, for each index you can search, its main sourcetypes, its events per day and its last event. The agent reads it with the first list in a request, so it runs fewer searches just to find where your data is. It is built once a day (the time is an admin setting) and is available on every edition. - If one of your roles filters which events you see, the catalogue shows you only index names, types and last-event dates, not sourcetypes or volumes. ### Fewer repeated searches across requests - Your own identical search from an earlier request is reused while Splunk still holds its results (10 minutes after it was last used), after checking it is still there. Nobody else's search is ever reused for you. - Word counts and the hours in which a word occurs are kept for 15 minutes and shared within your organisation, but only for indexes you can search, and never with or from a user whose roles filter events. - Time estimates and search budgets use the speed measured on each index, so the first estimate of a request is realistic instead of a fixed default. ### Searches rewritten to tstats, and shown - A dashboard's base searches (the shared searches its panels build on) and an alert's search are now also stored in the faster tstats form when that form gives the same result, as a saved search's already was. A base search that uses a filter token is reported, never rewritten. An alert whose trigger condition or e-mailed results depend on other columns keeps its search as written. - In the TOOL CALLS panel, a step whose search Adjutant rewrote says **changed by Adjutant**. Its details show the **Original** and the **Ran as** (or **Saved as**) search in full, each copyable, with the reason, and **Run original** asks the agent, as a reply, to run or save it as you wrote it. **Run original** is offered while the conversation is idle, not for a request opened from History. ### When no AI model is set up - **The `user` role can use the Console.** Before, a user with only the `user` role could not read the AI connections, so the Console offered none ("Configure LLM first") and Settings had nothing to show. The Console now gets the connections available to them from Adjutant AI's server, and their calls go through the Splunk server. **Settings** shows them **AI models available to you** (name, provider, model) instead of the connection list, which only people who may edit AI connections see. - **On opening the app**, a user with no AI connection available to their Org/BU sees a notice that names the Org/BU and asks them to contact their Splunk administrator (`admin` or `sc_admin`). This works for the `user` role too, which cannot list the connections. - **An administrator** who opens the app with no connection at all lands on **Settings** with the connection wizard open. If connections exist but none is available to their own Org/BU, a notice offers to set one up for it, and the wizard starts with that Org/BU chosen. - The notices show once per page load. When the connections cannot be read, no notice claims there are none. - **Settings** now says when the list of AI connections could not be read, with the reason. Before, a failed read showed "No AI connection yet." and offered to set one up, as if there were none. ### The LLM circuit breaker counts failures across requests - The LLM circuit breaker now opens after repeated failures across requests. Requests then go to the configured fallback configuration, or fail fast with a clear message, until a probe succeeds. - A paused configuration is tried again within two minutes at most: the longest pause (`default_circuit_max_open_duration_sec`) is now 120 seconds instead of 600. ### MCP servers: kept current, safer, and ready for gateways - **Daily refresh.** Every MCP server's tool list is read again once a day. A tool missing from one list is marked **missing upstream**; missing from the next day's too, it is disabled, and enabled again if it comes back. A failed or unreachable server changes nothing. **Refresh** still disables a missing tool at once. Agent templates that use a missing, removed or disabled tool are listed on the Tools tab and in a system message. `[mcp] daily_refresh = 0` turns it off. - **Headers.** The credential can go in a header of the server's choosing (**Auth header name**). **Static headers** are sent on every request; their values are kept in Splunk's credential store, never in the KV Store, and a credential typed into one is refused. - **Gateways.** A server can name a **Hook credential ref**, which the customer authorisation hook receives as `context["credential"]`. A hook that returns its headers with an expiry has them cached, encrypted, until 60 seconds before they expire; headers the server rejects are dropped and minted once more. OAuth servers can use client credentials, with an explicit token endpoint and an audience. - **Addresses.** Every request is checked before it is sent. Link-local and cloud metadata addresses are refused; a loopback address needs **Allow loopback**, which a server registered on loopback before 2.8.0 gets once at the upgrade; a redirect is followed only to the same host, and never from https to http. - **Load.** At most 4 requests at a time to one server from each search-head process; a 429 asking for 5 seconds or less is waited out once; a server with repeated outages is paused briefly. - **Names.** A server's short name is unique within its Org, and a tool's name wherever its scope overlaps another's. Existing duplicates keep working and are flagged. - **Import.** Tools the server marks destructive, or does not mark read-only, carry a warning in the import list. Imported tools still run without a per-call confirmation. - **Results.** What an MCP tool returns reaches the model fenced and labelled as untrusted data, and a large result is trimmed by whole records, with the number dropped. ServiceNow calls over MCP are logged with `run_id`, `adapter` and `read_as`. - **Failures are reported.** A refused update or delete of an MCP server or tool row now fails instead of reading as saved, and the change log records nothing for it. You get "Could not save MCP server" or "Could not delete server" ("Could not save imported tool" or "Could not delete tool" for an imported tool), a bulk import lists the tools it could not save, a refresh says how many tool rows it could not update, and deleting a server names any imported tool that could not be removed. ### Integration evidence, and three new dashboards - Every integration run, delivery receipt, verification verdict, refusal, watermark change and skipped run can be recorded as an event in an evidence index you create yourself: set `[integration_evidence] index`. It is blank by default, and then no evidence is written; an internal (`_*`) index is refused. An evidence event never holds the records themselves. - `[integration_evidence] require_for_live_writes = 1` refuses a live write to ServiceNow while no usable evidence index is set. The default, 0, lets the write go ahead, recorded as evidence not configured. - Three new dashboards for administrators read these events: - **Integration Ledger**: runs by state and the open runs, receipts with their delivery manifest, verification verdicts, watermark moves, refusals by reason and skipped runs, and **Runs with warnings**, each warning in words (for example a run that held its read position, or landed records more than once). - **Integration Status**: every integration job with its schedule, last run and a 30-day history. Click a job for its runs, with each run's warnings, and a run for every event of it in order. Without an evidence index the configured jobs are still listed. - **CMDB Quality**: the ServiceNow items Adjutant AI owns per class, classes two integrations both claim, items not landed for 7, 30 or 90 days, and the landings per integration with their verification verdict ("not checked" is never counted as verified). - A panel with no events, no evidence index set, or an index that does not exist says so; it never shows zero instead. ### Integration runs show their steps - The step view of an integration run now shows what the run did at each step: what was read, what each filter dropped, what the mapping produced, what routing refused and what was written, with the reason for each record that did not go on (for example an empty routing value, a destination not in the allowlist, or a missing key). A run that lands several resources or sources shows each of them separately. The run's history keeps the counts per step. - **Every integration run ends with its own record counts.** After the summary, the run says how many records it read, and how many were dropped by a filter, refused (with the reason), held for approval, written, or read and not landed. These are the run's own numbers, not the model's. When the model states counts that differ, the run says so as well, and its evidence records a `reply_counts_mismatch` warning. - **A count that does not add up is reported.** At each step of a landing, the records that went in must equal the records that came out plus those dropped, refused or held. When they do not, the run's evidence records a `counts_not_conserved` warning: that is a fault in Adjutant AI, not in your data. The write itself is never undone or held because of it. ### Fixed: a scheduled integration is recognised as one before it runs - **On a stateless installation, a scheduled integration whose read position was not restored after a boot is now held**, as the Stateless deployment guide describes (`skipped (no state)`, naming the missing position), unless the environment is new, a cold start was authorised, or the integration reads its whole source anyway. Since 2.5.9 such an integration started from the beginning instead, because the check did not recognise a scheduled integration. - **A skipped run of a scheduled integration is recorded in the Integration Ledger**: a run skipped because the previous one was still running, because the boot was not ready, or because a dependency had not completed. Before, these skips were not recorded, and the Ledger said that no scheduled run was skipped. ### Changed: a Splunk-source integration reads what its mapping says - **Adjutant makes the read itself.** An integration whose mapping reads a Splunk index is read from the mapping: the index it names, its filter and its fields. The first run, and every run of a mapping without a watermark, reads all time; once a watermark is declared, each run reads only the events indexed since the last verified run (see below). Before, the AI model wrote its own searches, and a search that did not name the index found nothing. - **A search the model writes itself is not run** in such an integration. The model names the resource and gets a reference to the records, never the records. If your integration's instructions tell the model to "search for…" the data, update them: the model is now told to ask for the read instead, and its own search is refused. - **Only new events are read.** A mapping that declares a watermark is read by index time: each run reads the events indexed since the last run it verifiably wrote, so a re-run no longer writes the same events again. `[agent_runner] splunk_read_lag_seconds` (300 seconds by default) keeps a read behind the indexers' clock, so events still being indexed are read by the next run. A run that reads its whole window and finds no new event moves its read position on, and says nothing about it: a quiet run is not a warning. When a run cannot move its read position forward (a write that failed or could not be verified, for example), its reply says so and why, and its evidence records it; the next run then reads the same events again. - **An empty read says why.** A read that finds nothing says how many events the index holds, for example "0 of 210 events in index=… matched `sourcetype=…`", or that the index has no events, and names its largest sourcetypes with their counts, so a filter that names the wrong one shows it. - **The filter is checked.** It takes field comparisons only, and may not name another index, a time range, a pipe, a subsearch or a macro. An index that does not exist is reported as such, not as an empty read, and already when you save, enable, run or verify the integration. ### Integrations that write the same events into an index again are flagged - An index cannot be updated in place, so an integration that reads its whole source on every run (a source without a watermark) and writes into an index writes the same events again on each run. Adjutant now warns about this in the mapping's lint, on the integration's page, when you save, enable or run it, in the run's evidence, and in a system message for administrators (at most once a day per integration). A mapping with a snapshot watermark is not flagged. - Events written into an index through the spool are checked for duplicates at the next run, once they are searchable: if the index holds any of the previous run's records more than once, the run says so, naming the previous run, and administrators get a system message (at most once a day per integration). Writes into a metric index (`index_metric`) are not checked for duplicates. ### Preview before write holds scheduled integration runs too - A scheduled integration with preview before write switched on now stops before it writes and shows its preview on the run, instead of stopping with nothing to approve. Approve the preview, then choose **Send approved payload**: a new run writes exactly the records you approved. - Sending an approved write sends exactly what was approved, even if new records arrived in the meantime; they follow in the next run. An approval is used once, and expires after an hour: an expired one is not sent, and the run shows a fresh preview instead. - When an integration names an approver role, anyone with that role in the integration's own organisation can see, approve and send its previews. Without a named role, only the person who started the run or an administrator can, as before. - Switching off the approval requirement for scheduled runs still lets them write without a preview. A scheduled reconciliation still needs that setting: it stops without a preview when approval is required. ### Reconciliation actions on the integration page - Administrators can now act on a reconciliation integration from its page: **Reconcile now**, **Test write access** per ServiceNow table, **Check relationship types**, **Change a record's key…**, **Request promotion**, **Export**, and **Preview** with **Push all records, not only changes**. - Promotions and key changes need two administrators: the requester sees **Waiting for a second administrator**, another administrator sees **Approve**, and either applies it once approved. - Going live, applying a promotion or key change, and deciding a held run each ask for confirmation first, stating the preview's own numbers and id. A push-all preview can now go live; before, it was refused as out of date. - A promotion or key-change request can be taken back with **Withdraw request** until it is applied, by the administrator who requested it or any other. A withdrawn request cannot be applied. Before, an approved request stayed open until it expired an hour later. - **Test write access** takes optional **Probe fields** for a table whose records need mandatory fields. Each field is checked against the table before the probe is written. - The page shows each test's and check's last recorded result when it opens: when, by whom, and whether it passed. - When an Organisation has no audit index, the pages say these actions are not recorded, and so does each action's result. Before, they ran unrecorded without a word. ### The change log records the server's writes to agents, skills and connections - Every write Adjutant AI's server makes to LLM connections, agents, skills, tool assignments, the knowledge library, the authoring audit log, ML models and the licence is now in the change log: a connection saved in the connection wizard, an agent the AI writes for a user, the shipped seeds and content packs, and the upgrade steps that rewrite these rows. Each write is read back. - Unattended runs written to the shared conversation history, the retention prune of their step payloads and the Observability pack's custom tools are logged too. A run written to an Org's own history collection (`per_org_history`) is not. - These events say where the change came from (`source`: `ui`, `llm_tool`, `seed`, `migration` or `system`). For agents, skills, tool assignments, the knowledge library's rules and the authoring audit log they hold the row as it was (`before`) as well as the row as it is. A connection's header values and a licence key are never in these events. - An edit saved on an Admin screen (the connection editor, Agents, Skills, Tools, Knowledge) is logged too, with who made it: the screens save through Adjutant AI's server. - When a connection the wizard or the connection editor saves still holds a credential in a URL it did not change, the save goes through and the field is named, so it can be moved to the credential field. - While a restore is running, a save on an Admin screen is refused and nothing is written: save again when the restore has finished. - The governance events in the Org audit index also cover the Admin screens' edits, a registered ML model, the licence (who activated or removed it; the licence key is never in the event) and Change Forensics source connections. A credential typed into a URL field named `endpoint`, or into a source's maps, is replaced by `[redacted]` there, as in a connection's URL fields. - Four new capabilities say who may change LLM connections (`adjutant_edit_connections`), agents and skills (`adjutant_edit_agents`), tools (`adjutant_edit_tools`) and the knowledge library (`adjutant_edit_knowledge`). admin and sc_admin hold all four, and so does a role named splunk_admin. The setup wizard sets up a shared connection for a holder of `adjutant_edit_connections`; a personal connection still needs none. On a licence without user authentication (Splunk Free), which lists no capabilities, the admin role can still edit. The Admin screens show the edit, save and delete controls only to a holder of the capability they need. When a save is answered by another version of Adjutant AI than the page was loaded from, the page asks to be reloaded. - The risk-scoring weight sets are in the change log, with their old and new weights. A restore is one change-log event per collection (`op=restore`, with the backup and the row counts). - A change saved without going through Adjutant AI's server (from a page opened before the upgrade, or a direct KV Store write) is found within 5 minutes and logged as `op=unlogged_update`, without who made it; a system message counts them. The first check after the upgrade only records the current rows. - Shipped agents and skills are added, brought up to date and retired by the server, when Splunk starts and then every 5 minutes, instead of when an administrator opens the app. Each of these writes is in the change log (`source=seed`); an agent or skill an administrator changed is still never overwritten. ### Records deleted outside Adjutant are held until you decide - A record a reconciliation integration published to ServiceNow, and that someone deleted there, is now held. Before, it was created again as soon as its source data changed, as a new record without its relationships, and a changed relationship was sent to the deleted record (Table API) or refused (IRE). - A held record is not sent, not retired, and its relationships wait. It is listed under **Deleted outside Adjutant** on the integration's page, and in the preview, with who deleted it and when. - An administrator chooses **Re-create** (the next live run creates it again and sends its relationships again) or **Forget** (it is never sent again; this cannot be undone in this version). Each decision is recorded in the audit log first. - Only a deletion the check is certain of is held. A record that may have changed class, or a check that could not read everything, is reported only. - `[recon] on_deleted_outside = report` keeps the earlier behaviour. ### Build and run integrations as flows - **Unattended → Flows** brings back the Integration Editor, and a flow you draw there now runs. Set each node's settings in the editor, save, and activate: a scheduled flow then runs on its schedule, and **Run now** runs it straight away. - **Run draft** is a dry run of the version you are editing: it reads and maps, shows its steps, and writes nothing. - The canvas shows how the last run went on every node. - A flow with an MCP trigger can be started by another AI agent over MCP, with the new `adjutantai_list_flows` and `adjutantai_start_flow` tools. Only administrators can use them. - A flow write held for approval can be approved and sent like an integration's: one preview for the whole run, then **Send approved payload** writes exactly what you approved to every destination. A send is refused when another version of the flow was activated in the meantime. - Activating, deactivating and running a flow are recorded in your organisation's audit log first; when that is enforced and the event cannot be written, nothing changes. - In this version a flow reads from ServiceNow, a Splunk lookup or a Splunk index, and writes through a mapping, or runs a reconciliation contract. Lookups and indexes are read as the business unit's service account when there is one, and only indexes that account can search are read. ### Two more ServiceNow write routes for reconciliation - A reconciliation contract can now write with **`all_ire`** (CIs and their relationships through ServiceNow's identification engine) or **`tables_only`** (through the Table API, without it), as well as `hybrid`. Before, only `hybrid` could be saved. - **`tables_only` runs attended only.** Unattended runs are refused for a contract with a `tables_only` view, at the request, at the approval and at every scheduled run; a person publishes each run. A run that loses ServiceNow's answer to an insert cannot adopt the record it created; the manual cleanup is in the reconciliation guide. - A ServiceNow mapping still writes through the identification engine only (`all_ire`). ### Agent Observability export - **Agent Observability export (off by default).** An administrator can send a trace of every finished agent question, including failed and refused ones, and background run to Splunk Observability Cloud or an OpenTelemetry Collector, from the new Agent Observability tab (Professional and higher). This release sends metadata only: agent, model and tool names, timings, statuses and token counts, never prompts, answers, SPL or results. A destination that is down or misconfigured never stops a question and delays it by at most 200 milliseconds. ### Change Forensics - A change collector records every Splunk configuration, app and deployment change on every host, with where it came from, whether and when it took effect, and when it was first used. Secret values are kept only as fingerprints. - The agent template *Change Forensics: what changed before it broke* and the **Change Forensics** Console tab rank the changes that most probably caused a problem with a deterministic scorer; a change counts only with a scope match, and each run writes one result bundle, once. - A Change Forensics run reports its verdict as "not applicable": it answers what changed, not a security question. Such runs are left out of the Outcome Ledger's figures (time to verdict and failed runs included) and the Automation Outcomes verdict chart, so they no longer count as investigations that could not decide. - Change Forensics needs the Splunk Platform edition (Enterprise or higher), Splunk Enterprise 9.4 or newer, and an index you create (`adjutant_platform`). The ledger's sourcetypes count against the Splunk licence. - Without the Splunk Platform edition the change collector collects nothing, quietly: administrators see a message about it only where the edition was licensed before and has lapsed. When the edition is back, the collector reads back the changes Splunk still holds from that period, and the coverage record names the period; anything older than Splunk keeps is named as not collected. - The agent template *Change Forensics: what changed before it broke* is ready to use (operational). On upgrade, an installed copy you have not changed moves to operational and keeps your own settings; a copy you changed keeps its state. ### Long-prompt prices - Some models charge more for a request whose prompt is longer than a set size, for example Claude Haiku 5.5 above 100K tokens and gpt-6-luna above 272K. Costs now use that higher price for each model call whose own prompt is longer. The other calls in the same request keep the normal price. Model pickers and the Models tab show such a model's price as "from $x". - Refreshing prices now also updates the long-prompt prices, and removes one the list no longer gives. The shipped prices include the long-prompt prices of 10 models, for each provider that sells them. - A price you set yourself with Set price on the Models tab applies at every prompt length. The list's long-prompt prices are not used for that model. - An install that refreshed its prices after 3 November 2026 keeps those prices after the upgrade, and gets the long-prompt prices at its next refresh. ### Splunk 10.6, unattended runs on every provider, and current models - **Splunk Enterprise 10.6 is supported.** Adjutant AI is supported on Splunk Enterprise 9.4.x to 10.6.x. Splunk 10.6's KV store writes small stored records, which can include conversation history and settings, to the `_internal` index: limit search access to `_internal` to administrators. - **Unattended agents run on OpenAI and Azure connections.** Alert-triggered runs, scheduled agents and agents started over MCP sent every connection a request in Claude's format, so a run on an OpenAI or Azure OpenAI connection always failed, and an OpenAI fallback could never take over from Claude. Each connection now gets a request in its own provider's format: Claude (Anthropic, and Bedrock through a gateway), OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Ollama and other OpenAI-compatible servers. A Gemini connection cannot run unattended agents in this version: the run fails at once and says so. - **Editing a Simple XML dashboard the agent built now changes that dashboard:** an edit to a Simple XML dashboard whose panels share one search used to be refused; it is now made to the same dashboard. When an edit is refused, the agent says the original dashboard is unchanged. - **Text with a NUL character is saved.** Splunk 10.6's KV Store refuses a NUL character in stored text, so a question, an answer or a search result containing one could not be saved, and the chat history save failed. In stateless mode, a decision a person made before 2.8.0 carries no record of who made it in the state store, so it can still expire there. - **Stateless mode waits longer for KV Store.** At boot, KV Store is now given up to 300 seconds to start (`kv_ready_timeout_seconds` in `[stateless]`), instead of a fixed 120. To remove them from search results, run the same search followed by `| delete`. Put the credential in the connection's credential field instead. The connection now keeps only the header names. On upgrade, the values are moved within five minutes: each one is stored and read back before it is removed from the connection, and a connection waiting to be moved answers "being moved" instead of calling without its headers. In stateless mode with `secrets_write = operator`, the app cannot store them itself: connections keep working with their old values, and a system message lists the credentials to create. In the connection editor a stored header shows its name only; leave the value empty to keep it. Downgrading to 2.7.6 after the move loses the header values; enter them again there. - **The KV Store change log no longer copies conversations.** The change log (`sourcetype=itmip:kvstore:change`, in `index=itmip_changes` unless you named another index under `[indexes] changes_index`) recorded the rows it tracked in full. For conversation history that was the whole turn: the question, the answer, the tool output and event text the tools returned. Now the change log keeps the row only for administrator settings; for conversation history, custom tools, MCP servers and knowledge connectors (updates only) it records who changed which row, how and when. Events already written stay as they are. Restrict read access to the change-log index to the people who audit the app. To remove the old copies, search over All time (use your index name): `index=itmip_changes sourcetype=itmip:kvstore:change collection IN (itmip_user_history, itmip_ai_knowledge_entries, itmip_llm_mltk_models, itmip_llm_license, itmip_llm_custom_tools, itmip_llm_configs, itmip_mcp_servers, itmip_knowledge_connectors) | spath output=old_before path=before | spath output=old_after path=after | where isnotnull(old_before) OR isnotnull(old_after)`, then run the same search followed by `| delete`. That needs the built-in `can_delete` role, which no user has by default, including admin; assign it for the cleanup and remove it afterwards. `| delete` makes the events unsearchable; they leave the disk when the index ages them out. - **A question gets an answer, not a new object.** When you ask about your data ("how many failed logins per user?"), the agent runs the search and answers. It creates nothing, and offers once to save the search as a saved search, an alert or a dashboard. It builds a saved search, alert, report or dashboard only when you ask for one, or accept that offer. A request that names one ("can you show me a dashboard of …") still builds it. - **A filter that starts at All offers All.** When a dashboard's dropdown or multiselect starts at All but its listed choices had no All among them, the list now starts with All. You can always return to every value after choosing one. - **A dashboard's help text matches what it does.** When the agent writes a how-to-read panel that describes the dashboard wrongly, the dashboard is not published, and the agent rewrites the panel. Examples: "click again to clear the filter" when a click only sets it; "click to filter" when no click filters; "applies to all panels" when a panel does not follow the filter. A filter set by a click is cleared with the reset row under the panel, or through its input. - **The answer is checked against what the tools did.** The agent rewrites an answer that misstates which panels share a search, how a dashboard's filter is cleared, an object's sharing, or whether an open page updates by itself. It also rewrites one that leaves out an object the request created. - **Tool calls: a saved search's step shows its validation.** The step shows the search that validated it, not the sizing search that ran after it. - **The answer is checked against what the tools returned, and what cannot be confirmed is shown.** Before you see an answer, Adjutant checks some of its claims against the tools' results. If a claim does not match, the agent gets one chance to correct it. 2.8.0 adds checks for four kinds of claim: - A saved search, alert or dashboard is said to work or to fire only when its check showed that. Describing the condition it fires on is always fine. - A filter is said to apply to every panel only when every panel uses it. - A host name, address or e-mail must come from a tool's result or from your request. - A dashboard's panel count, and a count of events, rows or saved objects of a named index, sourcetype or object, must match the result it describes. After that one retry, a link, name, address or figure that still could not be confirmed is listed under the answer as "Adjutant could not confirm this …". The answer text itself is never edited. Not every number is checked: only counts that can be tied to one result, about one in ten of the figures in an answer. - **A question from the agent ends its turn.** When the agent asks you something, it waits for your answer before it runs anything else. - **Two more agents revise the dashboard they built.** Build / improve an alert and AI Toolkit – Smart outlier detection (single metric) now change a dashboard they compiled with revise, as the dashboard agents do. A copy of either template that you edited keeps its own tool list: add splunk_revise_dashboard to it to get the same. - **A filter can apply to one tab or some panels.** When you ask for a filter on one tab, or on named panels, the dashboard applies it only there, and the answer names the panels it filters. - **Agents your licence includes are no longer shown as locked.** When the Console was opened before a licence was activated, or under a lower licence, agents that need a higher licence could stay locked after it was activated. A template's lock now follows the current licence each time it is loaded, and the upgrade removes the stale locks from the stored agents. - **The shipped models are the current ones.** The catalogue, the defaults and the connection checks now use each provider's current models: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (the default), Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1; GPT-6 Luna, Terra, Sol and Astra; Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite; GPT-OSS on Groq; the Claude 5.5 models on Bedrock; GPT-6 on Azure; Gemma 4, Ministral 3, Qwen 3.8 and Llama 4 on Ollama. Older models stay listed and priced for the connections that use them; retired ones are hidden. The connection check for Anthropic used a model Anthropic retired in February 2026 (Claude Haiku 3.5) and failed with "not found"; it now uses Claude Haiku 5.5. - **A connection can follow a model family.** A connection on Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini can name a family and then uses the newest version the catalogue holds and prices. In the connection editor and the Console the families come first, shown as "Claude Sonnet (latest) — currently claude-sonnet-5-5"; the versions follow under "Older versions", a model the provider still serves but no longer ships as current marked "(legacy)" and a deprecated one with "(retires )". A retired model is not offered. Pick a version to pin it. On upgrade, a connection on a model of a family moves to that family's newest version (for example Claude Sonnet 4.6 to 5.5, a dated version such as claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 to Claude Haiku 5.5, gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-4o-mini to GPT Luna, gpt-4o and gpt-4.1 to GPT Sol); one system message lists each connection, the old and new model and the new price. A new connection starts on its provider's family. The connection made from a v0.1 key now follows Claude Sonnet. - **A connection on a retired model is switched.** When a provider retires a connection's model, Adjutant AI moves it to the model's family or to the replacement the provider names, once that model is priced, and says so in a system message. Azure deployments are never switched: you are told to update the deployment in Azure. A connection that cannot be switched is named in its own message. In the Console, a turn started on a model that has since been retired uses the connection's current model, and one line under the answer says so; an administrator cannot save a retired model in the connection editor. - **GPT-6 models are sent the right token-limit parameter.** Like GPT-5, they refuse `max_tokens`; they are now sent `max_completion_tokens` from the first call. - **Dashboard agents work on Claude 5 models.** Claude 5 models, and Claude Opus 4.7 and later, refuse a `temperature` setting, and the agents that build dashboards set one, so each failed on its first call after a connection moved to a Claude 5 model. They are now sent no temperature, on the Anthropic and the Bedrock connections and through an OpenAI-compatible gateway such as OpenRouter. If another model refuses it, the call is repeated once without it. - **Asks work on gpt-6-luna.** GPT-6 models refuse the agents' tools while they reason, and every request to them failed on its first call. A request with tools now asks them not to reason (`reasoning_effort: none`). If another model or an Azure deployment gives the same refusal, the call is repeated once that way. - **Cached prompts on OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter and Gemini are costed correctly.** These providers count the cached part of a prompt inside its input tokens. Adjutant AI charged those tokens at the input price and again at the cache-read price, so the cost shown for a run that reused a cached prompt was too high. Cached tokens are now charged once, at the cache-read price, and the input token count shown for these providers is the uncached input, as it already was for Anthropic. Costs already recorded in History and Tokens & Costs are not recalculated. ### Dashboards, answer checks and MCP registration - **An automatic model switch updates the connection's last-changed time.** A connection that Adjutant AI moved to another model kept its old last-changed time; it now shows the time of the move. - **A dashboard on which every panel is empty is checked before it is published.** When the agent builds or revises a dashboard with its dashboard compiler and the render check sees every data panel come back empty over its time range, the dashboard is not published until the agent has looked at the data it filters on (for example, whether a field it filters on is in that data). It then fixes the filter or publishes the dashboard, and its answer must say that every panel is still empty and what the check found; the dashboard itself does not carry that note. A panel the check could not judge does not count as empty, and dashboards the agent writes directly as Simple XML are not checked this way. - **Time words in a request set the time range.** "Today" is since midnight, "this week" since Monday, "yesterday", "last week" and "last month" are whole periods, and "the last 24 hours" counts back from now. A dashboard built for such a request uses that range. A saved search or alert uses it when it sets a time range of its own; one that sets none keeps Splunk's default, and the agent is told which range the request named. When the agent deliberately uses another range, it is told to say why in its answer; the answer is not checked for that reason. The agent can set a chart's interval when a request asks "per hour" or "per day"; the request's words are not checked against it. Ranges such as "today" are worked out in the time zone of whoever runs the search: the viewer for a dashboard, and the owner for a scheduled search. A search shared to its app keeps its owner; only a search owned by nobody (for example one shared to all apps) uses the search head's time zone. - **A chart shows at most 10 values of a split.** A bar, column, line, area or pie chart split by one field (for example errors by component) draws 10 values, 5 on a pie. For a count or a sum these are the largest, and the rest are added up as OTHER. A time chart of an average shows the average of the rest's events as OTHER; of another aggregation, such as a maximum, it shows the rest together as OTHER. A category chart of another aggregation, or of several aggregations, leaves the rest out. Ask for every value by the split field's own name ("every component" for a split by component) to have them all drawn. Never capped: a search that sets its own limit, ends in `head`, `top` or `rare`, or has a stage after its last transforming command other than `sort`, `eval`, `fields`, `rename`, `fillnull` or `table`; a split by two fields; other chart types, such as a scatter chart; a panel whose search the compiler builds from one of its own patterns; and a split time chart that becomes the shared base search of several panels. Tables are not affected. - **A filter on a field the data does not have is named.** When a dashboard panel comes back empty, Adjutant AI checks whether each field its search filters on is in that data (the most recent 10,000 events of the panel's range; for a range that ends now, of its last 24 hours at most) and says which field is missing and which fields the data does have. A saved search or alert that filters on such a field is refused before it is saved, with the same finding; the agent can still save it when it gives a reason, for example a field that only appears during an incident. - **Build a Dashboard Studio dashboard is no longer in preview.** Every Ask user can choose it; in 2.7.6 only administrators saw it. On upgrade the shipped agent template becomes ready when an administrator next opens the app. One an administrator has changed keeps its own status, and copies made from it are not touched. - **Switching agents no longer carries your answers over.** An agent's question form you have not filled in is replaced when you pick another agent. When you have typed your own text in **Your request**, Adjutant AI asks first: use the new agent's form, keep your text, or cancel the switch. Before, the first agent's answers could be sent with the second agent's instructions. Switching the LLM, which ends the conversation, now also resets **Your request** to the selected agent's form (or empties it). - **The run status tool is enabled in Splunk MCP Server 2.1.0.** Splunk MCP Server 2.1.0 does not enable a tool whose description is too similar to one of its own, and it found `adjutantai_get_agent_status` too similar to its alert-action status tool, so the tool was registered but left disabled. The descriptions of the start, status and results tools are reworded, and the status tool is enabled at a following registration (within 10 minutes after the upgrade: the first round after a restart can skip). - **The MCP registration logs what actually happened, and names each tool it enables.** Right after Splunk restarted, Splunk MCP Server 2.1 could refuse to enable Adjutant AI's tools, and the registration still logged `registered`. Each enable now names the tool, and the logged action says what happened: `registered`, `partial` (some tools failed) or `failed`; each failure is listed (`index=_internal sourcetype=itmip_llm_mcp_register`). - **Two answer checks no longer send a correct answer back for rewriting.** A table's rank column (`#`, `No.`, `Rank`) is its position, not a count, so "| 1 | splunkd | 26,805 |" is no longer read as "1 event for splunkd". And a saved search or alert whose name has a word such as `_internal` counts as named when the answer names it, in bold or as a link. - **The MCP Example health check asks for a verdict the result contract takes.** It asked for healthy, degraded or inconclusive, and the contract takes none of the first two, so a run either picked another value, or recorded one the contract does not take. It now asks for benign (healthy), suspicious (degraded) or inconclusive. - **A run with no LLM connection says what to set for where it came from.** It always named the alert action's llm_config_id, also for a run started through MCP, which has none. An alert run still names the alert action, a scheduled run its job or integration, a REST run the request, and a run started through MCP or another path that uses only the default names the `[agent_runner] default_llm_config_id` setting. - **A zoom on a chart built with tstats zooms to the clicked bucket.** In Simple XML a click on a chart of `tstats … by _time span=1h` (or `bin _time span=` with `stats`) set a time range of one millisecond, because such a search does not say how wide its buckets are. The compiler now adds the bucket width to the panel's search, so the click zooms to that hour. A chart over `_time` with no fixed span (tstats' automatic span) cannot zoom in Simple XML and is refused by name; use timechart or a span. Dashboard Studio zooms by dragging across a range and is not affected. - **The render check of a Simple XML dashboard no longer reports a single value that is still loading.** A tile draws a preview while its search runs, and the check could read that preview as the tile's value, after which Adjutant AI told you a correct tile was wrong. The check now waits for the tile's search to finish (for a panel on a shared search, the shared search) within its time limit. A tile still running after that is reported as "the search was still running when the check read it; its value is not final", with no number, and is not compared with its data. - **A link in an answer is checked by its host as well as its address.** Adjutant AI's tools return links as paths on your Splunk instance. An answer that puts an invented host in front of such a path (`http://splunk/…`, `https://localhost/…`) is still refused and rewritten. A link to the same path on the address you opened Splunk Web with is now accepted. A path no tool returned is refused on every host. - **A dashboard can show two time windows again.** A request such as "the total over the last 30 days, and the count in the last 5 minutes" was refused every time, because the dashboard has one default range and the check held it to the request's last time phrase. Now the default may be any range the request names, and a panel can keep its own range in its search (`earliest=… latest=…`). A range no time phrase in the request names is still refused; a named range no panel uses is a note in the result, not a refusal. The dashboard's title and description may name the default range and any panel's own range, and "the last 30 days" also covers a range that starts at midnight 30 days ago (`-30d@d`). A dashboard was refused for saying the range it had. - **"Not published" now says which dashboard.** When the compile's attempts for one name were used up, its message said nothing had been published, even when a dashboard under another name had been published in the same conversation. It now names the dashboard that was not published, and says the others are not affected. An answer that says nothing was published while something was gets one rewrite. - **A "Sharing:" line in an answer is checked.** An answer that summed up a new private dashboard with "Sharing: app-wide." was not caught, because the line has no verb and does not name the dashboard. Such a line is now read as a statement about the object it is listed under. ### Security fixes - The SPL review no longer passes a macro's text to the model as Adjutant's own words. When the review expands a macro, which any user who may edit that macro wrote, the parts of its findings that quote the search (where each finding is, the suggested fix, and the findings table for a dashboard) reach the model marked as untrusted data, so an instruction written into a macro is read as data. A search you type yourself, with no macro, reads as before. - The ITSI root cause analysis view and the fraud readiness view no longer place what is typed into, or linked to, their text boxes directly into their searches. The run fingerprint from an e-mailed link and the index pattern are now quoted and escaped, so a crafted link cannot add its own search commands, and the fingerprint shown on the page is escaped too. - A configuration package can no longer carry a credential. A package with a password, secret or key in any of its files (also a commented-out one, or a value shaped like a known key or token) is refused, naming the file, line and setting, never the value. Field extraction patterns that mention passwords stay allowed. - A run started over REST (`POST /services/itmip_llm/agent/run`) can no longer pretend to come from another source. The run counts as a REST run unless the request names an alert source (an Enterprise Security notable, an ITSI episode or a native alert); any other source is refused. Before, a caller could name an internal source and so choose a different path or time budget for the run. - A search the assistant writes can no longer read Splunk's credential store. Run as an administrator, `| rest .../storage/passwords` returns the stored secrets themselves, including Adjutant's own AI and connector keys, and the assistant's search can be steered by the data it reads. Such a search is now refused in the Console and in unattended runs, in every form (`storage/passwords` under any app or user, `authentication/users`, `conf-passwords`, encoded or inside another search). Other `rest` searches in the Console are unchanged. The agent template "AI Toolkit – Score against an AWS SageMaker endpoint" no longer builds a credential check panel on that search; its dashboard now says where to look when the endpoint's credentials fail. - Passwords, secrets, keys and access tokens are now removed from what a tool returns before the assistant reads it, in the Console and in unattended runs, and so never reach the AI provider, the conversation history or the audit log. This covers fields named for a credential (such as `clear_password`, `client_secret`, `api_key` or `hec_token`), `password=` and `"password": "..."` pairs inside events, and values shaped like a known key or token. The assistant is told how many were removed ("[redacted: 2 credential fields]"). Token counts such as `tokens_in` are not affected. - Searches the assistant writes are checked more strictly before they run. In a question in the Console, a search may no longer use `mcollect`, `meventcollect` or `dump`, which write metrics, events and files (unattended runs already refused them). In an unattended run, where searches run with the administrator's rights, a search the assistant writes may no longer use `savedsearch` or `loadjob` (they run another search's text unchecked), `dbxquery` or `dbxoutput` (they can change an external database) or `deletemodel`. Adjutant's own searches are not affected. - Azure OpenAI endpoint discovery now sends a connection's stored key or token only to the connection's saved host, never follows a redirect, and is for those who may edit AI connections only. Before, a user allowed to use an Azure connection could have its stored credential sent to a host they named. - Only someone who may edit AI connections, or the owner of a personal connection, can record, reset or start a connection check. Before, any user could do it for any connection by calling it personal, and so change the status badge others see. - Sharing a trained AI Toolkit model with every app now works only on your own model, unless you are a Splunk administrator. Before, any user could make another user's private model global. - A connection's key and header values now reach the browser only for people who may edit AI connections. Everyone else's calls to a connection set to call from the browser now go through the Splunk server, which must be able to reach the provider; if it cannot, the message says so and what to ask your administrator. Before, every user allowed to use such a connection received its key in the browser. - The list of models available in the Console no longer names, to everyone, the AI connections that use each model. Only people who may edit AI connections see those names; before, every user saw the connections of every Organisation and Business Unit. - Calls through the Splunk server now always use the stored connection's provider to decide how its key is sent, and a disabled connection is no longer called. Before, the request could choose the provider, and so the way the stored key was sent to the connection's host. - An integration can no longer write one of Adjutant AI's own KV Store collections, such as the LLM connections, agents or skills. Before, a destination allowlist with a pattern (`itmip_*`), or a record that names its own destination, could reach them and overwrite them without a change-log event. Each record is checked, and the others in the batch still land. The collections the shipped network-policy and Observability mappings write into stay allowed. Collection names that begin with `itmip_` are reserved for Adjutant AI: an integration that wrote into a collection of your own with such a name is now refused, so give that collection another name and allow it instead. - The store of integration writes waiting for approval is checked to be closed to administrators before it is read or written. An install whose permissions for it were changed by hand, which overrides the shipped ones, could otherwise keep the pending payloads readable by other roles. - Every credential Adjutant AI stores (LLM connection keys and headers, MCP server headers and tokens, the licence, network device and Observability credentials) is now readable by administrators only. Before, only Splunk's `list_storage_passwords` capability kept other roles from reading them. Connection keys and headers, MCP server headers, the licence, the scheduled-job signing key and network device credentials stored before the upgrade are restricted once, at the next start; the others when they are next saved. An entry you created yourself, such as one your customer authorisation hook reads, is left as it is. A run goes through five steps: 1. **Stage** each source's rows into a holding area. 2. **Accept** a source's data as a whole, or reject it as a whole: enough rows, a usable key on every row, no duplicate keys. A read the source reports as **truncated**, or one that lost more rows than the contract allows, is still accepted for what it saw — but it is never used to decide that something is gone. 3. **Reconcile** the accepted data.
