Both are off by default. **Changed** - The retry setting is now called **`runner_max_attempts`** (it covers every kind of failure, not only runaway runs). The unused `retain_completed_hours` setting has been removed — run history retention is controlled by `queue_retention`. If you set either in a local override, update it. --- ## 1.8.5 "CIM Coverage Audit" When a data source is onboarded but a correlation search in Enterprise Security still comes back empty, or an ITSI KPI never fills, the cause is almost always that the source is not properly mapped to the CIM data model the search depends on. Finding out why is normally a slow, manual walk through the layers. The CIM Coverage Audit does it for you, from your real events and your real search head configuration. **New** - **Audit a sourcetype against a CIM dataset.** Ask, for example, audit cisco:asa against the Network Traffic All_Traffic dataset. You get back how much of the dataset the source covers, and if it does not, which layer is broken: the source is not tagged so the model cannot see it, its index is not on the model's allowlist, a field is missing or under the wrong name, a value needs normalizing, or the accelerated summaries the correlation searches read have not caught up. That last one is the confusing case where CIM works when you test it by hand but your correlation searches fire nothing, and the audit calls it out plainly. - **A fix you can read and deploy.** For each gap the audit produces the exact configuration, checked for validity, shown as your current stanza next to the proposed one, with a note on where it belongs. It never deploys anything itself. You review and apply it, which is what lets you run this where an automatic write to production would never pass change control. - **Honest about what a search head can see.** Adjutant AI runs on the search head, so it reads your search time configuration and the real events, and it is upfront that it cannot read the index time configuration on your indexers. It runs its searches as you, so it can never read data from an index you could not otherwise search. - Three read only helpers to read a sourcetype's search head props and transforms and check where a sourcetype has data. The diagnosis is available on Professional so any platform team can see which layer is broken. Generating the validated fix is an Enterprise feature. It grades against the CIM add on actually installed on your search head. Restart Splunk after upgrading. **Fixed** - **The app opens on the Ask tab again.** If your LLM runs entirely on the search head, with the key held server side (the Splunk proxy mode, an Azure managed identity, or a Bedrock role), the browser never receives an API key. The app opens on Ask, and sends you to Settings only when a key really is needed and missing. - **Clearer license status.** When a license is installed but the app cannot confirm it is active on this environment, it now tells you that directly instead of quietly dropping to the free Personal tier. Admins get a pointer to the License page to re-activate. --- ## 1.8.4 "Async playbooks over MCP" Run Adjutant AI playbooks from an AI agent over the Model Context Protocol with a reliable **start → poll → fetch** pattern. A playbook can take several minutes, but AI tool calls are subject to short timeouts you don't control (the MCP server, the client, proxies), so trying to wait for the answer in one call is fragile. Now every call returns in seconds. **New / Improved** - **Start returns immediately.** `adjutantai_start_playbook` (the old `adjutantai_run_playbook` name is removed) hands back a run id at once with a hint on how to poll. - **Check progress** with `adjutantai_get_playbook_status` — queued, running, completed, or failed (a run that hit a recoverable error and is auto‑retrying is reported as still running, not failed), with guidance to stop polling after ~15 minutes. - **Fetch the verdict** with `adjutantai_get_playbook_results` once completed — condensed by default, or the full result on request; a partial result is clearly labelled. - **Tenant‑safe.** One team can't read another team's run; unknown or expired run ids simply return "not found." Run records are kept for 7 days by default. - **Try it out of the box:** start `MCP Example: Read-only Health Check` under Org/BU `DFLT/DFLT` (the read‑only reference playbook shipped on every install), then poll and fetch. Requires the inbound MCP server and the Backend Ask Service to be enabled. No configuration changes. Restart Splunk after upgrading. ### Also in 1.8.4 — the Outcome Ledger (Enterprise) A single screen that answers what a CEO, CISO or auditor actually asks: *what did agentic AI do for us this period, was it any good, what did it save, what did it cost — and can I see the evidence for one run?* It assembles data the app already records (unattended‑run history, analyst agreement, run telemetry, LLM spend) into one executive/audit view. It adds **no new data collection and sends nothing to any external service.** **New** - **The dashboard** (`Adjutant AI ▸ Outcome Ledger`): headline tiles (investigations run without a human, how often analysts agreed with the AI — with the sample size and coverage shown, benign/false‑positive runs auto‑closed, analyst hours saved, LLM spend, typical time to a verdict), the mix of AI conclusions over time, agreement by case type, a weekly ledger, and an **evidence** table you can click through to the full detail of any single run. A footer spells out every assumption so a number is never quoted out of context. - **Safe to hand to an auditor.** What each viewer may see is decided on the server from their own identity — never from the page — and fails closed. In this release the dashboard is for Splunk administrators. - **Is the AI real, or just performing?** An Efficacy Trend panel puts run volume against how often analysts agreed, over time. If the agent runs more while analysts increasingly override it, the panel says so ("scaling faster than trust") instead of hiding it behind a healthy‑looking headline — and on too little feedback it honestly says the sample is too thin to judge. - **Honest numbers.** Effort saved is shown as time (with the per‑case assumption stated), spend is the real logged cost, and the per‑investigation efficiency signal is token usage — never an invented cost estimate. Enterprise feature. No effect on any existing behaviour. Restart Splunk after upgrading. --- ## 1.8.3 "Security hardening" A security‑focused release. Adjutant AI was put through an independent OWASP Top 10 (web **and** LLM), dependency‑vulnerability, and "AI‑driven ransomware" review. The headline: **no critical issues, no default passwords or keys, no vulnerable components that ship to you, and the assistant cannot be turned into an attack tool.** Confirmed issues are fixed. **Improved / Fixed** - **Credentials stay server‑side.** Provider API keys and keyless Azure sign‑in secrets are never sent to the browser or to other users in your tenant. (The free‑tier browser API‑key path is unchanged.) - **Prompts stay in your audit index**, not Splunk's internal logs. - **Stronger multi‑tenant isolation** for investigation results and knowledge sources. - **You confirm every change.** Closing a notable, setting a disposition, an ITSI/TrackMe/ServiceNow write, or overwriting a saved dashboard now asks for explicit confirmation first. Read‑only questions and new private dashboards are unaffected. - **General hardening:** cleaner errors, tighter sign‑in redirects, safer content‑pack imports, email TLS verification on by default. No new features or config changes. Restart Splunk after upgrading. --- ## 1.8.2 "Edge Processor data-quality + keyless Azure OpenAI auth" **Keyless Azure OpenAI (Microsoft Entra ID / managed identity).** Connect Azure OpenAI **without a static API key** — using a Microsoft Entra ID service principal or a managed identity, governed by your Entra tenant. Runs entirely server-side (no token reaches the browser), supports Public and US Gov clouds, and adds a one-click **Test connection** that names exactly what to fix if something is off. Connecting Azure with a plain **API key** still works on every tier; the keyless Entra path is an **Enterprise** capability. --- ### Edge Processor data-quality If your data passes through **Splunk Edge Processor** before it reaches Splunk, some parsing, timestamping, dropping and routing happens *upstream* — where Splunk's own internal logs and feed-health tools can't see it. This release teaches the assistant to look at that hop. - **New "Edge Processor → Splunk data-quality check".** Ask the assistant to check an Edge Processor feed and it reads Edge Processor's own operational metrics (throughput, dropped events, failed destination sends, and queue backpressure) and tells you, in plain language, whether data is being silently lost or delayed before it lands — with a proof dashboard. - **Honest by design.** If Edge Processor telemetry isn't reaching your Splunk yet, the assistant says so and gives you the exact setup steps (on-premises vs Splunk Cloud) instead of inventing a clean bill of health. It reports at the pipeline level and is clear that per-event checks need a small addition to your Edge Processor pipeline. - **Folds into the readiness verdict.** Edge Processor joins Splunk parsing, feed-health, and Cribl as another "is this data actually good?" signal, and can cap the Data Quality Score when it finds upstream loss. - Read-only and available on every tier, exactly like the existing Cribl check. --- ## 1.8.1 "Cleaner support diagnosis" A small maintenance update over 1.8.0 (front-end only). - **More accurate "Report an issue" diagnosis.** The automated issue classifier no longer mislabels a session that finished normally — one that completed and produced its dashboard — as having "run out of tool steps." The suspected-issue summary in your support bundle is now cleaner for healthy, tool-heavy sessions. --- ## 1.8.0 "Agent telemetry & OCSF export, content packs & all-tiers data quality" **New — your SOC can watch the agent (OCSF telemetry).** - **Adjutant AI emits its own activity as OCSF.** Every LLM call, tool / MCP / ServiceNow call, configuration change, unattended run verdict, and **policy refusal** (the proof the controls actually fire) can be written as open-standard **OCSF** events to a Splunk index your Enterprise Security / SOC already watches — mapped to CIM via the community **OCSF-CIM Add-On**. Your SOC monitors our agent the same way it monitors everything else: on-prem, with no cloud egress. - **You stay in control.** It is **off by default** and Enterprise-gated. **You provision and name the index** (the app ships no `indexes.conf`). Routing and content are resolved **per Organisation / Business Unit**; content export is denied by default and never exceeds your audit (DPIA) ceiling, with a server-side redaction check before anything is written. - **See it immediately.** A shipped admin dashboard — *Adjutant AI — Behaviour (OCSF)* — shows the token trend, model mix, tool/MCP egress with identity, the refusal and finding feeds, and a per-run drilldown, all on raw OCSF (no CIM Add-On required). **New — update Adjutant's content without waiting for a whole new app release.** - **Content packs.** Almost everything Adjutant does well lives in its **content** — the skills, knowledge, and playbooks. A **content pack** is a single, versioned file that lets us ship a corrected or improved content set straight to your install, and lets your admin apply it safely — no Splunkbase re-vetting cycle for a content fix. - **Your changes are protected.** Applying a pack **upgrades only the items you haven't changed**. Anything your team has customised is left exactly as-is and clearly listed, never silently overwritten — and your Org/BU scoping is always preserved. After an import you get a per-item report, and the list of items that need manual reconciliation is downloadable as a CSV. - **Safe by design.** Every pack carries an integrity check, so a tampered or truncated file is refused. Imports live on the **Backups** page, which also shows which content version you're currently on — run a backup first and you can roll back in one click. - **Retire without deleting.** A pack can mark an item **retired** — it stays installed but is hidden and switched off everywhere (it can't be picked, run, or used by the assistant). An admin can re-enable it at any time by removing the tag. **Improved — data-quality checks for everyone, and Splunk 10.x readiness.** - **Data-quality ingestion checks are now available on every edition, including the free tier.** Checking whether a feed is actually landing and parsing correctly — on `index=_internal`, through **TrackMe**, and through **Cribl Stream** — is a baseline capability now, not a Professional add-on. - **Ready for Splunk Enterprise 10.2 and 10.4.** The app declares Python 3.9 **and** 3.13 compatibility and has been audited against the 10.x platform changes (dashboards, the web framework, KV Store). Your admin still completes the standard KV Store engine migration as part of any 10.x upgrade. - **Smarter Dashboard Studio building.** The assistant now works from a single, version-aware map of what Dashboard Studio supports on **your** Splunk version — it won't reach for a chart type your version can't render, and when your Splunk is newer than what we've documented it builds conservatively and verifies the result. **Fixed.** - **A slow dashboard is recognised as working.** For a heavy Dashboard Studio dashboard, the assistant confirms whether the panels returned data before deciding it is blank, so no retry is spent on a dashboard that is correct. A genuinely blank dashboard is still caught. - **TrackMe panels only when they belong.** The assistant adds a TrackMe feed-health panel only when it is relevant, using a method that works in your app. --- ## 1.7.0 "ServiceNow integration" (included in the 1.8.0 release) > **Renamed to Adjutant AI.** The app is now **Adjutant AI** (formerly "AI Workbench"). > This is a **display-name change only** — the in-app title (the easter egg now lives on > the dot of the "i" in **Adjutant Ai**), the app label, the documentation, and the > assistant's own self-description all say **Adjutant AI**. Nothing functional changed: > the Splunk app id, your saved searches/dashboards/models, KVStore data, and generated > artifact names are unchanged, so the upgrade is seamless. **New — run playbooks automatically, and from other Splunk apps.** - **On a schedule or on an event.** A playbook can run **unattended** on a schedule (a "morning health check") or in response to a Splunk event — an alert, an ES correlation search, or an ITSI episode. When an event triggers it, the affected thing (the host, user, or entity in the alert) is handed to the playbook automatically, so it investigates exactly what fired. Two ready-made (disabled) examples are included to copy. - **Adjutant AI as a building block for other apps.** Other Splunk AI agents can now ask Adjutant AI to **list** and **run** your playbooks through a small, safe interface (an MCP server). Only playbooks you mark **MCPready** are exposed, every call must name the Org/BU it is for (which must be a business unit you have set up) as a safeguard, and runs go through the same governed, bounded service — never an open door. This interface is **off by default** — turn it on with one setting. When on, the tools can also appear inside **Splunk's own MCP Server**, reachable on the normal Splunk web address (no special port needed); you authenticate with a standard Splunk token. A ready-made, read-only **example playbook** ships enabled so there is always something to see the moment you switch the interface on. **New — "Report an issue" support packaging (all editions).** - One click on any conversation (per-turn 🐞, the Ask panel, or the new **Help tab**) packages exactly what happened — versions, the resolved prompt, the tools and model used, the generated dashboards/searches, and every error and warning — into a single file. - **Safe by construction:** secrets are stripped before anything leaves the browser, and the file is **encrypted** to the support key, so it's safe to send over any channel. - It even **tells you what kind of problem it looks like** and matches known issues, so simple cases are solved without a back-and-forth. - **Send it your way:** download it and attach it to your own ticket, use the built-in support form, or email it. The **Help tab** (Report + Documentation + About) is always reachable — even if the app is locked by licensing. **New — ServiceNow, done properly** (Professional + the `servicenow` feature). Read incidents, changes, problems and the **CMDB/CSDM** in plain English — with bounded blast-radius / dependency traversals ("what's the blast radius if this CI fails?"). Turn a Splunk alert, ITSI episode or ES notable into a rich, deterministically rendered ServiceNow incident and **write the number back** to the originating object (a re-fire updates, never duplicates; the closed-incident policy is configurable). **Security incidents (SIR)** with MITRE ATT&CK, off until an admin enables them. Two transports (REST **or** a ServiceNow MCP server), plus TISC threat-intel enrichment — all server-side and allowlisted, so ServiceNow can never block the assistant. *(Verified against the documented APIs and unit-tested; final certification is on a live ServiceNow.)* **New — run playbooks automatically, and from other apps.** Playbooks can run **unattended** on a schedule, or from a Splunk alert / ES correlation search / ITSI episode (the triggering entity is handed to the run). Adjutant AI can also expose **list / run** over an inbound **MCP server** (off by default, MCPready-only, Org/BU-scoped) — reachable inside Splunk's own MCP Server on the normal web address, with a standard Splunk token. **New — "Report an issue" support packaging (all editions).** One click packages a failing conversation — secret-stripped and **encrypted client-side** — with an automatic problem classification, plus an always-reachable **Help tab** even when the app is licence-locked. **New — Cribl Stream data-quality awareness** (Professional+). Reads Cribl's own forwarded logs and metrics to surface the timestamp / parse / dropped-event problems that happen *inside Cribl, before Splunk can see them* — the "green in Splunk but timestamped wrong" blind spot — folded into one readiness verdict. No Cribl Lake or Search required. **New — LLM reliability: retry, fallback & circuit breaker** (Enterprise). A brief provider hiccup (503 / 529 / rate-limit) auto-retries within a time budget; a per-config **circuit breaker** stops hammering a provider that's down, then probes for recovery; and an ordered **fallback** transparently switches to your next provider (and tells you which it used). Two new admin dashboards — **LLM Health** and **AI Activity** — plus per-user / BU / org concurrency caps, all conservative and off the critical path. **New — live model & cost catalogue (all editions).** Models and prices come from a runtime catalogue that updates without an app rebuild; **automatic model discovery** (Professional+) keeps it current without ever logging your keys; an Enterprise admin screen adds price overrides and manual model registration for private gateways. **Fixed.** Generated Simple XML dashboards now share a single base search across panels (faster) and get a top data-ingestion health panel; corrected a 3× Opus price over-charge (now server-side authoritative, with Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 included). --- ## 1.5.0 "Data Foundation & MCP OAuth" **New:** connect to **OAuth 2.1‑protected MCP servers** (authorization‑code + PKCE for interactive, client‑credentials for unattended; tokens held server‑side, never in the browser — see [MCP_OAUTH.md](MCP_OAUTH.md)); **onboard new data sources** — describe a source or attach a sample file and get a deployment‑ready add‑on package; a **"is my data parsed correctly?"** ingestion/timestamp check that reads Splunk's own internal logs; generated config **validated against your instance** and given a **0–100 Data Quality Score** (A–F); and attach a local sample file in Ask (only the file name is audited, never contents). **Improved:** works with the newest OpenAI "reasoning" models incl. Azure GPT‑5.4 / GPT‑5.4‑mini (auto‑detects the request format); more reliable generated dashboards; generated objects use the **`aiworkbench`** name tag; and Audit‑tab improvements (Business Unit column/filter, local‑timezone timestamps, reliable token/outcome capture). --- ## Earlier releases (1.0.0 – 1.4.3) - **1.4.3** — Clearer guidance and plain-language fixes when a free-tier LLM key hits its provider limits (e.g. Groq token-per-minute caps, Gemini zero-quota keys); the LLM config screen flags these up front. - **1.4.1** — Per-feature capability licensing with edition badges (Professional / Enterprise / MSP); gated features show a padlock, and nothing you created is ever deleted when a tier changes. Turn-level audit logging made reliable; more robust dashboard generation. - **1.4.0** — The assistant reads your own Splunk **live** (real search commands + installed visualizations) instead of guessing; Splunk Security Essentials detection content integrated. - **1.3.3** — TrackMe integration end-to-end (feed-health awareness + actions) with richer built-in platform knowledge. - **1.3.2** — First Splunkbase 1.x release: packaging and permissions hardening. - **1.3.1** — Fixed Org/BU edits dropping fields; safeguard to keep bundled playbooks correct after upgrades. - **1.3.0** — Real, per-Organisation audit logging of every AI interaction (Professional+). - **1.2.0** — Splunk Security Essentials content tools for playbooks. - **1.1.1** — Cisco Deep Time Series Model (CDTSM) playbooks: pre-trained anomaly detection and forecasting via the AI Toolkit, each with a proof dashboard. - **1.1.0** — Multi-tenancy and the Organisation / Business-Unit editor overhauled for clearer, safer tenant scoping. - **1.0.0** — The knowledge layer: ground answers in your organisation's own conventions. *(Releases before 1.0 are early pre-release history and are omitted here.)* --- ## Known issues - **Open the assistant from inside another app.** Adjutant AI is a "host shell": reach it from a navigation-menu entry inside Search, Enterprise Security, ITSI, or your own apps — not by clicking the app tile directly. Everything it creates lands in the namespace of the app you opened it from. - **Some Data Foundation features need self-hosted Splunk.** The configuration-reference grounding and config-package generation (1.5.0) read files on the Splunk server, so they are unavailable on Splunk Cloud; the assistant says so and continues with what it can. - **A record deleted outside Adjutant comes back when its source changes, without its relationships (since 2.7.0).** A live run that has a change for such a record creates it again in ServiceNow, as a new record. Its relationships are not sent again while they are unchanged, so the new record does not get them. A relationship that changes before the record comes back is sent with the deleted record's id when it is written through the Table API, and is refused when it is written through IRE. To keep a record deleted, remove it from its source too. --- *When a published fix resolves a tracked GitHub issue, it is summarised here with its issue number — for example: "Fixed: a dashboard panel could display raw HTML markup as text instead of formatting it (#123)."*


Short Description:
AI agents that run inside your own Splunk, on the model you choose, including a local model with Ollama, so nothing has to leave your network. Ask in plain words and get a search, dashboard or alert that is run before it is saved. Once you switch it on, an agent investigates the moment an alert, ES notable or ITSI episode fires. Free for one user, no licence key.


Description:
Your Splunk team can do far more than it has time for. Adjutant AI gives them that time. Adjutant AI puts governed AI agents on the Splunk you already run. It ships with 67 ready-made agent templates, so you install it and start the same day: no prompts to write, no project to run. What changes for your team - Security analysts get back to the hard cases. Agents triage Enterprise Security notables and alerts with asset, identity and risk context, so your people start where the agent stopped. - Everyone else stops waiting for the SPL expert. Describe what you need in plain words and get a working search, dashboard or alert, checked on your own Splunk and owned by you. - The Splunk admin team finds problems sooner, and at lower cost. Agents check feed health, data quality and CIM coverage, explain any search with real row counts, and trace an ITSI service problem to its root cause from the data itself. - Managers can see what happened. Every step is shown live and can be stopped, every action is gated, and on Enterprise every run is audited. Your first week 1. Install the app and connect the AI model you choose: a cloud provider, or a local model on your own network for air-gapped sites. 2. Open the Console and run a ready-made agent on your own data: build a dashboard, explain a slow search, check a feed. 3. Switch on the agents that should work by themselves. When an alert, a notable or an ITSI episode fires, the investigation is already waiting when someone opens it. Be the team that got there first Splunk is one of the most valuable platforms in your organisation. Adjutant AI lets you show it: requests handled on the spot instead of in a ticket queue, investigations that start by themselves, and a Splunk team known for what it delivers. While others are still deciding whether AI belongs in their Splunk, you are already using it, under control. Built to be trusted Each agent works with the asking person's own Splunk permissions. Your keys stay on your side, and your data goes to no model but the one you choose. Runs on Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud, alongside Enterprise Security, ITSI, the AI Toolkit, TrackMe and ServiceNow. Some agents need the Professional or Enterprise edition. Free for one user to build searches, dashboards and alerts, with no licence key needed. Your model, your network: Ollama or another local model, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock and more. Keys stay in Splunk's secret store, and nothing is sent to us. Get started in three steps: install, connect your model with the setup wizard, ask your first question. Free for one user. For your team, request a 30-day Professional key: https://www.thedutchdatadifference.nl/contact/. Documentation: https://docs.thedutchdatadifference.nl/adjutant-ai/

item.title: Whisper Security Infrastructure Graph Add-on - v2.0.1 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
# 2.0.1 release notes 2.0.1 fixes what several commands return and what the dashboard and Configuration page say. It adds no command and removes nothing. Install it over 2.0.0. Your account, API key and data-sharing acknowledgement carry over. Answers cached by 2.0.0 are not reused: each command asks Whisper again, and the first `whisperenrich` search clears 2.0.0's rows from `whisper_graph_enrichment`, the collection its automatic lookup reads. It runs on Splunk 10.2 and 10.4 with `python.required = 3.13` only, as 2.0.0 did. ## New * `whisperlookup evidence=true` adds `whisper_other_lists` (popularity lists, allowlists and other lists that are not threats) and `whisper_unclassified_lists` (listings Whisper has not classified). `whisper_sources` now holds threat feeds only. * `whisperenrich` domain rows carry `whisper_geo_country` and `whisper_geo_city`, for the address `whisper_asn` describes. ## Improved * The Investigate dashboard lists threat feeds apart from other lists, and names the allowlisting behind a benign verdict, such as a popularity rank. * Its tables no longer show rows no search fills, such as RPKI and MOAS. * `whisperflush mode=expired` and `whisperevict` also clear expired rows from `whisper_graph_enrichment`, with one result row per collection. * The Account tab's upgrade count also looks for `whisper:threat_intel`, `whisper:watchlist`, `whisper_domain_lookup` and `whisper_ip_lookup`, and runs again on your first save after the upgrade. * Each `whisperenrich` search logs its last request id for Whisper support. ## Fixed * On a `whisperenrich` domain row, `whisper_is_threat` is the domain's own verdict, as on `whisperlookup`. 2.0.0 read `true` if any of its addresses was flagged; that count is in `whisper_is_threat_address_count` with `detail=full`. * `whisper_registrar` and `whisper_prev_registrar` show the registrar's name, such as `MarkMonitor Inc.`, not an id such as `iana:292`. A domain that never changed registrar no longer gets the registrar-change risk factor. * `whisper_cname_target` is the last name in the CNAME chain, the same on every run. * If Whisper declines to score an indicator or sends no answer, `whisper_threat_score` reads `N/A` and `whisper_threat_level` is empty, where 2.0.0 could show `0.0` and `UNKNOWN`. An indicator with no data still reads `UNKNOWN`. * With `detail=full`, `whisper_threat_feed_ids` lists threat feeds only. * A `whisperenrich` row with no answer reads `whisper_status=degraded` with `context-incomplete` instead of `ok`. Rows answered under an API key Whisper did not accept read `degraded` with `key-not-accepted` in `whisperenrich` and `whisperschema` too. `whisperenrich` caches neither. * An empty `whisperschema` answer returns one row instead of none. * An empty `whisperquery` query says the query is empty instead of refusing it as a write. * An install upgraded from 1.0.0 with a user name and password in its hidden proxy URL can save the Settings tab again, and the save deletes that URL. The password was stored in clear text: change it on the proxy, then use the Proxy fields. * On Splunk Cloud, a refused Test connection asks for the time of the test and its message, not a request id the page does not show. * The packaged README and the `whisperenrich` help match what the add-on does, and the package drops an unused command-line helper from a bundled library.


Short Description:
Answer who runs an IP or domain, what shares its infrastructure and whether anyone has reported it, from the Splunk search bar. Five search commands, eight macros and one dashboard over Whisper Security's graph of internet infrastructure. No index, no scheduled search, no modular input. Needs a free API key.


Description:
An IP address or a domain lands in your search results and you have ten minutes to decide whether it matters. Who runs it. What else sits on the same infrastructure. Whether anyone has reported it before. This add-on answers those three questions from the Splunk search bar, against Whisper Security's graph of internet infrastructure: DNS, BGP, WHOIS, hosting, mail records and threat feeds, joined as one connected structure rather than a set of separate lookups. What you get: five search commands. whisperlookup puts a coverage-qualified verdict on events you already have. whisperenrich attaches the infrastructure behind an indicator to those same events: routing and network, hosting, and feed listings. whisperquery runs a parameterised Cypher query and returns the rows as events. whisperschema describes what is in the graph. whisperflush manages the local cache. Eight macros answer the next questions without any Cypher: the verdict for one indicator and the graph's own explanation of it, registered look-alike domains, whether a hostname's CNAME points at a service nobody holds any more, registration history, and the CNAME and SPF chains. The eighth makes no call: it turns the two fields below into a word for a results table. One dashboard, Investigate, opens a single hostname, IP address or URL in three bands: the verdict and what it rests on, the network that routes it, and the neighbouring hosts that share its address. Every row says how sure it is: two separate fields, and neither stands in for the other. Coverage says what the graph knows about the indicator, with one of six values: Evidence of malice; Contested evidence; Listing stopped; Not answered; No data; or Checked, not malicious. Call status says whether the request that asked completed, and carries the sentence for what to do next. An empty panel is an answer about the indicator, not a failure of the add-on. What it needs: a Whisper Security API key, free from https://console.whisper.security/sign-up?source=splunk-addon-listing. Outbound HTTPS to graph.whisper.security on port 443. Splunk 10.2 or later, on a search head. Setup is one page: enter the key, tick the box that authorises indicators to leave your deployment, save. The key is held in Splunk's encrypted storage/passwords and nowhere else. What it never does: it writes to no index and ships no indexes.conf. It ships no modular input and no scheduled search, so it makes no call out of your deployment unless someone runs a search. It claims no CIM mapping, because it indexes nothing to map. It ships no detection content. Until an administrator ticks the consent box, every command in the deployment sends nothing and says so on the row.

Release Notes:
**Release notes for Splunkbase (version 1.10.0)** - Builds work again after pip 26.3. TA Studio now holds pip at a working version during builds. Thanks to nterl0k for tracking this down. - New: upgrade an add-on's libraries to the Python your Splunk runs. Add-ons whose libraries are locked to an older Python can be moved to Python 3.13 from the Reconciliation page. - Imported add-ons are safer to edit: field aliases keep all their pairs, CIM mappings no longer copy settings between source types or add tags you didn't choose, and setup tabs keep the add-on's own account table. - Source types, lookups, event types and saved searches no longer gain default settings when saved. On some source types those settings could change how events are split. - Validate now runs additional AppInspect checks. - Builds add `python.required` everywhere AppInspect requires it, including search commands, scripted inputs, scripted lookups and REST endpoints. - Opening an installed add-on no longer copies its local settings, such as saved passwords and configured inputs, into the project or the build. - Fewer ways to lose work: leaving a page, switching tabs or going Back with unsaved changes now asks first. - Deploy never leaves Splunk without the app: the new copy replaces the old one only once it's fully in place, and leftovers are cleaned up or reported. - Clearer build errors, including for add-ons whose libraries were built for an older Python. - The Reconciliation page no longer reports problems that the build fixes by itself.


Short Description:
Build, import, validate, and package Splunk add-ons through a visual browser UI — no CLI. Create inputs (REST/shell/Python), alert actions, source types, field extractions, CIM mappings, lookups, and setup pages on the UCC Framework, run inputs and alerts in the browser to inspect their output, validate with AppInspect, and package for Splunkbase in one click.


Description:
TA Studio is a browser-based visual workbench for building Splunk® add-ons (TAs) on the Universal Configuration Console (UCC) Framework — without touching the command line. Authoring a quality add-on normally means working with the ucc-gen CLI, hand-editing globalConfig.json and a web of .conf files, and running AppInspect and packaging from a terminal. TA Studio replaces that workflow with a guided, point-and-click interface that runs entirely inside your own Splunk instance. From one UI you can create and manage data inputs (REST API, shell command, or Python modular inputs), alert actions (including Enterprise Security adaptive response), source types, field extractions with a live regex builder, CIM data model mappings, setup pages (accounts, proxy, logging), CSV lookups, and event types. You can import existing Splunk Add-on Builder and conf-based add-ons to modernize them, run inputs and alert actions right in the browser to inspect the events and output they produce, validate with AppInspect (including cloud checks) and review the results, then package a Splunkbase-ready archive in one click. TA Studio also includes built-in AI assistance to help you generate and refine input and alert-action code as you work. It otherwise runs entirely within your local Splunk environment: your add-on projects are not collected, transmitted, or stored outside your instance, and AI features send only the content you choose to submit to your selected AI provider.

item.title: Hurricane Labs Add-on for Windows PowerShell Transcript - v0.2.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\## 0.2.0 Tested on Splunk Enterprise 9.4.3, 10.4.1 and 10.6.1. Supports Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.x transcripts. \### Fixes \- Events are now timestamped with the session's Start time instead of the transcript file's last-modified time. \- PowerShell 7 transcripts ("PowerShell transcript start") now split into one event per session, and their end blocks are dropped. CRLF and LF files both work. \- Transcripts in other languages now parse: Windows PowerShell 5.1 on non-English Windows and PowerShell 7.6.6+ translate the header, so parsing now goes by the header's layout instead of English words. \- user, domain, username, runas_user and runas_domain keep dots, spaces and $ in names, and handle NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. \- std_out now starts after the header for both PowerShell versions. \- computer/dest no longer spans several lines when the machine name is blank. \### Eventtype changes (search time) \- powershell_encoded_command matches every -EncodedCommand abbreviation (-e, -ec, -enc ...) and the / forms (/e, /enc ...), but only when followed by a base64 UTF-16LE payload. -Encoding abbreviations and other tools' -e (docker, git, sed) no longer match. \- powershell_command needs -Command (or -c, -com ...) on a line that runs powershell or pwsh. -ComputerName, -ComObject, Invoke-Command, Get-Command, python -c and bash -c no longer match. \- powershell_nslookup_txt also matches -type\=txt and -querytype\=txt. \- powershell_registry also matches Get-ItemProperty -Path HK... and Set-Location HK... \### New \- CIM Endpoint.Processes field names: dest, process, process_id, process_path, process_name, action. \- powershell_transcript_session eventtype for opting in to the CIM Endpoint data model (no data model tags by default; see the README). \- Splunk Cloud readiness: \[id] stanza in app.conf and sc_admin write access. \### Upgrade notes \- Timestamp, line-breaking and end-block changes apply only to newly indexed data. \- Eventtype changes apply at search time, so they change what existing saved searches and alerts on these eventtypes match. \- Events are now dated by session start, which can be well before Splunk receives them. Scheduled searches with short lookbacks should search by arrival time, e.g. \_index_earliest\=-20m. \- Transcript times have no time zone. A single forwarder reading transcripts from several time zones needs a per-host TZ (see the README). \### Known limitations \- A session is one event, and Splunk drops everything past 256 KB (TRUNCATE), so commands after very long output aren't indexed. \- Command output that reproduces a transcript header (e.g. Get-Content of another transcript) splits the session there, and later commands take that header's fields and start time. \- Full list in the README.


Description:
This app provides knowledge objects for working with Windows PowerShell transcript logs. In addition to field extractions, a number of event types are included to support threat hunting use cases. You will need to configure your Windows systems to log PowerShell transcripts in order to benefit from this app. This logging is not enabled by default in Windows. These logs, once generated, should be collected via a file input and forwarded to Splunk. Additional information on the configuration of this app is available here: www.hurricanelabs.com/splunk-tutorials/splunk-tutorial-powershell-transcription-logging This app is also available on GitHub: https://github.com/HurricaneLabs/TA-powershell_transcript

item.title: Jamf Pro Add-on - v3.0.4 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
# Jamf Pro Add-on for Splunk — Changelog *** ## Version 3.0.4 > **Compatibility Note:** This release requires Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud Platform **10.2 or later** (i.e., Splunk versions that support the Python 3.13 interpreter.) > > Jamf is no longer publishing a Python 3.9-compatible version of this add-on via Splunkbase. Python 3.9 is end of life and continued support would require the inclusion of Python packages that have unpatched vulnerabilities and outdated cryptography libraries. Additionally, Splunk Cloud 10.6 drops 3.9 support entirely and the current version of Splunk AppInspect will not permit Splunkbase release of add-ons pinned to Python 3.9. If your Splunk environment only has Python 3.9 available, you'll need to upgrade Splunk before installing this or future versions of the add-on. Please contact Jamf Support if you are unable to update to a modern version of Splunk. ### Updates The only change is moving the Computer Inventory input from the `v1/computers-inventory` Jamf Pro API endpoint to the more modern /v4 endpoint. The structure of the JSON data returned by the v1 and v4 endpoints is similar so most reports and queries should continue to work without change, with one notable exception — the date-time when a device last contacted Jamf Pro. * /v1: `general.lastContactTime` * /v4: `general.lastContact` We felt it would be confusing if we patched a key to something other than what the API documents to maintain backwards compatibility. Therefore, we've chosen to store this key as the Jamf Pro API provides it. As a result, if you have queries that reference this key, update them to use the new key name. If you have a time-series analysis that looks at a computer's records over time that references this key, use the coalesce function to ensure that your query works no matter which API version sourced the event: `| eval last_contact \= coalesce('general.lastContact', 'general.lastContactTime')` *** ## Version 3.0.3 ### Bugs Fixed * **JSON fields from Computer and Mobile Device inventory are now extracted and searchable.** Events from the Computer Inventory and Mobile Device Inventory inputs are indexed as JSON, but their sourcetypes were configured so Splunk performed no field extraction — the raw event was visible in search results, yet individual fields (e.g. computer name, hardware, operating system, extension attributes) could not be searched, filtered, or reported on. All `jssUapiComputer:*` and `jssMobileDevice:*` sourcetypes now use JSON key-value mode, so their fields are parsed automatically. This is a search-time change, so fields are also extracted from events that were already indexed before the upgrade — no re-indexing is required. ### Maintenance * The add-on version is now defined in a single place (`globalConfig.json`) and propagated to every other file (app metadata, package, and the Jamf Pro User-Agent) at build time, so the reported version can no longer drift between them. *** ## Version 3.0.0 Version 3 is a major release. **The accompanying** [**Upgrade Guide**](Splunk-Add-On-for-Jamf%20Pro_v3-Upgrade-Guide.md) **should be reviewed before installing this version.** ### Splunk Version Compatibility * Migrated from Splunk Add-on Builder (AOB) to the Universal Configuration Console (UCC) framework. * Upgraded Python runtime from 3.9 to 3.13. All bundled packages are now resolved at build time against Python 3.13, replacing cp39 compiled extensions that could not load under Splunk Enterprise 10.2. ### New Features * **Account-driven credentials.** Jamf Pro URL, username/client ID, and password/secret are now configured once on a separate Account settings section and referenced by name from each input. Create, edit, and test accounts on the new **Configuration → Accounts** tab. * **In-place upgrade from v2.12.x.** On first run after upgrade, the add-on automatically migrates each existing input into the new account-driven model. * **Test Credentials button** on the Account form. Probes the Jamf Pro instance with entered credentials and returns verified/invalid/error feedback before save. Enforces HTTPS and rejects private/reserved/metadata IP ranges (SSRF protection). * **Explicit Authentication type dropdown** on the Account form (`API Client` or `Username + Password`). Replaces the 2.x convention of prefixing the username with `client:`; accounts upgraded from 2.x are auto-corrected on first run. * **Test Endpoint button** on the Custom API Query input form. Probes the configured endpoint against stored credentials before save, so typos are caught at edit time rather than via silent post-save failure. * `skip_unchanged` checkpointing on Computer and Mobile Device inputs. The add-on remembers each record's content hash between polls and suppresses events for records whose payload is byte-identical to the last fetched copy. * **Unified input error reporting.** Every operator-actionable failure from any input writes an event to both the add-on's input log and a searchable `sourcetype=jamf:input:error` index event. Each event carries a `category` field — `config`, `auth`, `endpoint`, or `record` — for filtering and alerting. * **Event time format** option on the Computer Inventory input: choose between time of import, last inventory update, or last contact time. * **Auth Type column** in the Accounts table shows "API Client" or "User Account" at a glance. * Daily polling (86400 seconds) is now the default interval for all three inputs. ### Security * To guard against proxy-in-the-middle attacks, TLS certificate validation is now enforced on all connections to Jamf Pro. If your Jamf Pro server still uses a self-signed or private CA certificate, either update your Jamf Pro to use a publicly-trusted certificate or install your private certificate authority's trust chain in your Splunk server's CA-Cert store before upgrading. ### Bugs Fixed * Many errors arising from incorrectly-configured inputs have been remediated. Error handling and logging have been modernized across the add-on.


Description:

Release Notes:
\# Log Monitoring 3.15.0 This release is for upgrades from 3.12.2. It also contains 3.13.0, 3.14.0 and 3.14.1, which were not published separately. \## New \*\*Bulk actions on Log Outage\*\* \- A new Select column at the start of the table. Tick rows one by one, or use Select this page. \- Bulk action applies one action to all selected rows: Delete alert, Undo delete alert, Passive alert, Change threshold, Clear threshold override, Disable monitor or Re-enable monitor. \- Each action is applied only to the rows where the row menu would offer it. Before anything is saved, the dialog lists those rows and counts the ones it skips. Afterwards it reports how many rows changed, and lists any row that did not change, with the reason. \- Up to 200 rows at a time. Disable monitor, and any action on more than 20 rows, asks you to type the number of rows to confirm. \- After a bulk action, Undo puts the rows back as they were. It does not touch a row that someone has changed since. Undo is available until the page is reloaded. \*\*Admin Guide page\*\* \- A new page in the menu for the tasks that are done in the lookup files: stopping monitoring of an index, a sourcetype or a host. \- For each task it shows which lookup file to edit, the exact row to add, what happens, and how to undo it. \- It also lists everything that is stopped right now, read from those lookup files. A suppression that has no effect, because its reason is empty or its date cannot be read, is marked NOT ACTIVE. \- The page only reads; it changes nothing. \## Changed \- The Collector runs every 3 minutes instead of every 5. It still looks back 8 minutes, so one missed run leaves no gap. If you have set your own schedule for this search, yours is kept. \- New installs use a 4-hour outage threshold for all sources. Before, it was 24 hours, and 1 week for syslog sources. Existing installs keep the values in their \`dvlm_settings.csv\`. An empty value now falls back to 4 hours. \- The Index lists on Log Outage and Stream Health no longer show indexes set to \`off\`. \## Fixed \- Setting an index to \`off\` in \`dvlm_index_config.csv\` used to stop only data collection. The sources already tracked for that index stayed on the pages and turned Critical. They no longer appear as outages and raise no alerts. Their old rows stay in the collection until Maintenance Purge removes them. \## Upgrade 1\. Install over the existing app. The package contains no lookup files, so your lookups and decisions are kept. 2\. Optional: to use the 4-hour default, set \`default_threshold_sec\` and \`syslog_threshold_sec\` to 14400 in \`dvlm_settings.csv\`. 3\. If Log Outage does not show the Select column, reload the page without the browser cache. No saved searches, lookups, KV fields or permissions were added or removed. \## Known limitations Unchanged since 3.12. See README.txt. \## Rollback Reinstall 3.12.2. Your lookups and decisions are kept.


Short Description:
Detects log delivery outages per index/sourcetype/host by tracking arrival time and diagnosing whether the forwarder agent or source stopped delivering.


Description:
Log Monitoring detects log delivery outages on a per-index, per-sourcetype, per-host basis by tracking arrival time and diagnosing whether the forwarder agent or the source itself has stopped delivering data. The app uses scheduled searches to record the most recent arrival time for each source every five minutes and computes outage status at read time, eliminating the need for manual inventory maintenance. Detection is based on arrival time rather than event time to avoid false positives caused by clock skew or timestamp parsing failures. The app distinguishes between three failure modes: an agent that has stopped running, an agent that is running but not forwarding data, and a source that has genuinely stopped producing logs. This diagnosis relies on independent liveness signals from Splunk internal logs and deployment server phone-home data. All tracking data is stored in KV store collections and CSV lookups, with no custom indexes, Python code, scripted inputs, or custom commands required.

When enabled, the action succeeds with `response_received` set to false if the question has not been answered yet, instead of failing. If the question can no longer be answered (expired, timed out, or an unknown question ID), the action still fails. Defaults to false, so existing behavior is unchanged. * Added the `expire question channel with blocks` action. It closes an unanswered question asked with `ask question channel with blocks`: it marks the question expired so later clicks are rejected, then edits the posted message to remove the buttons and show a timeout message. The question metadata is removed only after the edit succeeds, so a failed edit can be retried. If the question was already answered, the message is left unchanged. * `get response` now fills `summary.question_id` and `summary.response` when a response is available. * `ask question channel with blocks` now also stores `message_ts` and the posted `blocks` in the question metadata, for use by `expire question channel with blocks`.

Release Notes:

Short Description:
Free honeypot threat intelligence for Splunk. Enrich the IP addresses in your events with a verdict, ASN, ports and first and last seen, index free threat feeds of exploiter IPs and malware URLs, and query the honeypot dataset by CVE, payload, network, or JA4, Akin and HASSH fingerprint. No account needed to start.


Description:
HoneyLabs Intelligence is a free Splunk app for honeypot threat intelligence. It enriches the IP addresses in your own events with what HoneyLabs honeypot sensors recorded from them, indexes free threat feeds of active exploiter IP addresses and malware download URLs, and queries the honeypot dataset by port, payload, CVE, network, and JA4, Akin or HASSH fingerprint. HoneyLabs runs honeypot sensors on the public internet. No real user has a reason to connect to them, so the traffic they record comes from scanners, brute-force tools and exploit attempts looking for exposed systems. An address reaches the exploiter feed only when a sensor captured it running an exploit or a loader command, and known research scanners are left out. Every indicator links to its evidence at honeylabs.net/lookup. Getting started needs no account. Open the app's Setup page and turn on the threat feeds with one click each. Each feed is pulled every hour and needs no API key. The Triage dashboard then matches your traffic against them and lists hosts in your network that contacted captured malware infrastructure, followed by inbound connections from addresses seen running exploits. The honeylabs command enriches any event that carries a public IPv4 address: index=firewall | honeylabs field=src_ip | where honeylabs_events > 0 It adds a verdict, first and last seen, country, ASN and network owner, reverse DNS, the ports the address targeted and its exploit hits, each field prefixed honeylabs_. Addresses are de-duplicated per search, so a scanner that appears in ten thousand events costs one lookup. The honeylabssearch command queries the honeypot dataset directly. Its modes cover raw sensor events, captured request payloads, top attackers, timelines, IP, CIDR and domain lookups, CVE exploitation, ASN profiles, and fingerprint activity and population. Use it to see who else probes a CVE, what payload they send, or which sources share a JA4 fingerprint. The feeds and enrichment work without an account, and anonymous enrichment allows 10 lookups a day. A free API key from honeylabs.net raises that to 500 credits a day and is required for honeylabssearch and the Explorer dashboard. Pro allows 50,000 credits a day and Team 500,000. The key is stored through Splunk's storage/passwords, encrypted at rest and never written to a .conf file. A lookup sends only the public IP addresses in the field you name. Private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses are filtered out before the request is built, and no other part of the event leaves your deployment. The feed inputs are plain HTTPS downloads and send nothing about your data. With Splunk Enterprise Security, load the same feeds through the ES threat intelligence framework so indicators reach correlation searches and risk scoring. The guide at honeylabs.net/integrations/splunk-es has the field mappings.
